note: Medieval / Old West / Old Timey are Extras flags tested via 0x020867ec(flags, n); each assigns a gear-slot actor part through 0x020063d4(actor, part, 0). Recovered by tools/export_customization_modes.py.

medieval.predicate_input: actor byte +0x6bb, now established to BE the runtime character id
medieval.evidence_for_index: 0x0200f508 indexes the 24-byte descriptor table at 0x020ef57c with actor byte +0x6bb scaled by 0x18, the same table the portrait join indexes by runtime id - so the two are the same number

enhanced_modifier_clarifications.scope: These concern the silly setting modifiers - Old West, Medieval, Old Timey - which are ENHANCEMENTS planned after parity, not part of the Bounty Hunter baseline. Recorded now so they are not lost or half-remembered later.
enhanced_modifier_clarifications.source: Clarifications made while reviewing out/work/modifier_check.png, from first-hand knowledge of the original game.
enhanced_modifier_clarifications.evidence_tier: PLAY - first-hand knowledge of the original game's behaviour, not yet cross-referenced against the ROM.

old_west_weapon.WRONG: Classic Blaster is NOT the weapon Old West mode gives.
old_west_weapon.CORRECT: Old West gives REVOLVER PISTOLS - the kind Jango Fett and Han carry.
old_west_weapon.why_it_matters: A modifier that swaps in the wrong weapon model changes silhouette and animation, and Classic Blaster is a visibly different prop from a revolver.

hats_and_hair.behaviour: A hat applied to Leia does NOT remove her hairpiece - both render together.
hats_and_hair.contrast: Customize and Extra modes DO remove the hairpiece when a hat is applied.
hats_and_hair.why_it_matters: So hat-on-head is not one rule. The modifier path keeps the hair; the customize and extra paths strip it. Implementing a single shared rule would be wrong for one of the two.
